Digital Filters: Pole-Zero Design, Notch, Comb, Allpass and Inverse Systems (L09)

Why this matters in the exam: L09 has never been tested. Sample Test 1 covered only L02–L04, so filters are fresh material for the final. Tutorial 8 is the only practice set, and its five questions show the likely pattern: design FIR coefficients from constraints (T8 Q1, Q3), find nulls in Hz (T8 Q2), read a response off a pole-zero plot (T8 Q4), and find a stable inverse (T8 Q4c, Q5). Sample Test 1 split 20 marks into parts worth 4–7 marks, so expect a filter question of about 4–7 marks, often chained (design, then check, then invert).

1. The core ideas

1.1 Filtering and the ideal filters (L09 slides 4–8)

For an LTI system, . is a spectral shaping function. It is periodic in with period , so you only ever need .

  • Low frequencies sit at (near ).
  • High frequencies sit at (near ).
Ideal filter Passes Rejects
Lowpass (LP)
Highpass (HP)
Bandpass (BP) everything else
Bandstop (BS) everything else

Ideal filters have in the passband and in the stopband. They are not realisable (their impulse responses are infinitely long and non-causal). You use them to describe what you want, then approximate.

  • Trap: a DT frequency is always in rad/sample. To get Hz use . Going the other way, .

1.2 Linear phase and group delay (L09 slides 9–10)

  • What it is: linear phase means every frequency is delayed by the same samples. The output is just a delayed copy of the in-band input. Nonlinear phase causes phase distortion.
  • When you get it: an FIR filter with symmetric coefficients, , has linear phase with . For 3 taps that means and delay 1 sample. For an -point moving average, delay .
  • How to show it: pull out the centre delay. Example: . The bracket is real, so the phase is (plus where the bracket is negative).
  • Trap: the jumps where the real amplitude changes sign do not spoil linear phase. The course writes if , and otherwise (T8 Q1). Group delay is still constant.

1.3 Pole-zero patterns (L09 slides 12–14)

The magnitude at frequency is set by distances from the point on the unit circle:

A pole close to the unit circle at angle makes a peak at . A zero on the circle at makes .

Type Poles Zeros
Lowpass near unit circle, near () on/near unit circle near ()
Highpass near unit circle, near () on/near unit circle near ()
Bandpass complex-conjugate pair near circle, inside passband often at or
Bandstop / notch (optional) just inside the zeros on the circle

Poles at do not change (they are distance 1 from every point on the circle). They only add delay.

  • In z: , so . Every pole and zero moves to (reflect through the origin). A zero at moves to .

1.5 The named filters

Filter Poles / zeros Use
Resonator (slide 17) poles , ; zeros (or both at 0) bandpass, vowel synthesis
FIR notch (slide 19) zeros ; double pole at 0 kill one frequency
Pole-zero notch (extension) zeros , poles narrow notch, flat elsewhere
Comb / moving average (slide 21) zeros , ; poles at 0 kill a frequency and its harmonics
Allpass (slide 23) or , , poles and zeros are reciprocals: phase equaliser
Oscillator (slide 25) poles on the circle generate a sinusoid

This is the Example 2 notch (, poles at just behind the zeros). Drag the poles towards the zeros and watch the notch narrow. Drag them to the origin and you get the wide FIR notch of T8 Q3.

1.6 Inverse systems and phase type (T8 Q4–Q5; builds on L08 slide 8)

The inverse system undoes : , so

Poles of = zeros of . Zeros of = poles of . Stability of therefore depends on where the zeros of are.

Recall from L08 slide 8: a system is stable iff its ROC includes . A causal system is stable iff all poles are inside the unit circle.

For a causal, stable (all poles inside):

Zeros of Name Stable inverse is Its ROC
all inside unit circle minimum phase causal
all outside unit circle maximum phase anti-causal
some inside, some outside mixed phase (the course says nonminimum-phase, T8 Q5b) non-causal (two-sided) ring between them
any on the unit circle (e.g. notch, comb) no stable inverse exists none contains
  • Trap: “the inverse” usually means “the causal inverse” (T8 Q4c) unless the question says “stable inverse” (T8 Q5c). Read which one is asked.
  • Trap: the inverse of an FIR notch has poles on the unit circle. It is an oscillator, not a stable filter. You cannot “un-notch” a signal.

1.7 The stable non-causal inverse via partial fractions (needed for T8 Q5; not on the L09 slides)

This uses the L08 slide 4 rule for each partial fraction, with the ROC chosen so that it contains the unit circle:

Why: the stable ROC is the ring that contains . For a pole inside the unit circle, the ring lies outside that pole, so its term is causal. For a pole outside the unit circle, the ring lies inside that pole, so its term is anti-causal. Both terms decay away from , so is absolutely summable.

Partial fractions in (the course’s form):

  • Factor the denominator into .
  • Cover-up: .
  • If the numerator degree in equals the denominator degree, add a constant = (last numerator coefficient)/(last denominator coefficient). T8 Q5 has .
  • Check: , which is the ratio of the coefficients of numerator and denominator (usually 1). For an FIR you can also check .

  1. . Factor numerator and denominator of .

4. Traps that cost marks

  • Mixing up and . A null at “50 Hz” with Hz is at , not 50. Answer null frequencies in the units asked (T8 Q2 wants Hz or rad/s).
  • Comb filter with the wrong length. The nulls are at , where is the number of taps. T8 Q2 has , which is 5 taps, so nulls at 200 and 400 Hz, not 250 and 500.
  • Normalising at the wrong frequency. T8 Q3 asks for at (substitute ), not at DC. Normalising the FIR 50 Hz notch at DC instead gives huge gain at high frequency.
  • Losing linear phase in the algebra. Write the phase as with jumps where the real amplitude changes sign. Don’t write everywhere, and don’t call the jumps “nonlinear phase”.
  • LP→HP sign flips in the wrong place. Only odd powers of change sign, in both numerator and denominator.
  • Wrong ROC for the inverse. Causal inverse: outside all poles. Stable inverse: the ring containing . A pole outside the circle gives . The minus sign is easy to drop.
  • Forgetting the constant in an improper partial fraction. If the degrees of numerator and denominator are equal (T8 Q5), there is a term.
  • Calling a filter with zeros on the unit circle “minimum phase”. A notch or comb has no stable inverse at all.

7. Add to your open-book reference sheet

L09 DIGITAL FILTERS
w0 = 2*pi*F0/Fs  (rad/sample);  F = w*Fs/(2*pi);  Omega = w*Fs
|H(w)| = |b0| * prod(dist to zeros)/prod(dist to poles); poles at 0 don't change |H|
LP: poles near z=1, zeros near z=-1.  HP: reverse.  BP: poles r e^{+-jw0}.
Linear phase: theta = -w*n0 ; tau = -d theta/dw ; symmetric FIR -> n0=(N-1)/2
  phase may jump by +-pi where real amplitude changes sign (still linear phase)
LP->HP: h_HP(n) = (-1)^n h_LP(n) ; H_HP(z)=H_LP(-z) ; flip odd powers of z^-1 ; p -> -p
FIR design: H(w)=b0+b1 e^{-jw}+b2 e^{-j2w}; null H(w0)=0; DC: sum b=1; pi: b0-b1+b2=1; lin phase b0=b2
Notch (FIR):  b0(1 - 2cos(w0) z^-1 + z^-2)
Notch (IIR):  b0(1 - 2cos w0 z^-1 + z^-2)/(1 - 2r cos w0 z^-1 + r^2 z^-2); width ~ 2(1-r) rad
Resonator:    b0(1 - z^-2)/(1 - 2r cos w0 z^-1 + r^2 z^-2)
Comb/MA:      (1/(M+1)) (1 - z^-(M+1))/(1 - z^-1); nulls F_k = k Fs/(M+1)
              |H| = (1/(M+1)) |sin((M+1)w/2)/sin(w/2)|, phase -Mw/2
Allpass:      z^-N A(z^-1)/A(z); poles/zeros reciprocal; 1st order (a+z^-1)/(1+a z^-1)
              tau(w) = (1-a^2)/(1+2a cos w + a^2)
Oscillator:   b0/(1 - 2cos w0 z^-1 + z^-2); b0=sin w0 -> h(n)=sin(w0(n+1))u(n)
              y(n) = 2cos w0 y(n-1) - y(n-2) + b0 x(n)
INVERSE: H_I = 1/H ; poles of H_I = zeros of H
  zeros all inside  -> minimum phase    -> stable inverse causal
  zeros all outside -> maximum phase    -> stable inverse anti-causal
  mixed             -> nonminimum phase -> stable inverse non-causal (ring ROC)
  zero ON circle    -> no stable inverse
STABLE INVERSE h_I(n): partial fractions A_i/(1-p_i z^-1), A_i = [(1-p_i z^-1)H_I]_{z=p_i}
  |p_i|<1 -> A_i p_i^n u(n) ;  |p_i|>1 -> -A_i p_i^n u(-n-1)
  equal degrees -> + K delta(n), K = last num coef / last den coef
  check: sum A_i + K = H_I(z->inf)
